newsitem.title: CANADA: HORSE RACING-IN THE BREEDERS' CUP, IT'S CIGAR AND THE REST.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-IN THE BREEDERS' CUP, IT'S CIGAR AND THE REST.

text.p: The Breeders' Cup is designed to keep all eyes, minds and wallets lasered onto thoroughbred racing's orgy of $11 million up for grabs in seven races Saturday.
The annual spectacle will still be a frenzy of betting on the horde of superstar horses shipping in from around the world for the sport's annual showcase.
But all talk, flashbulbs and newsprint has been focused on one six-year-old, who Saturday at Woodbine likely will end one of the most storied careers ever.
"Cigar boards the plane. Cigar walks off the plane. Cigar parades around the barns. Cigar rolls in the hay. Cigar eats a peppermint candy. Cigar wiggles his rear end in contentment."
That's the kind of attention heaped this week onto the horse, whose run at the great Citation's record 16 consecutive victories lit up the racing world.

Cigar's streak was stopped at 16 last August in California by Dare and Go, who is expected to be the biggest threat to send Cigar into stud with a loss in the Breeders' Cup 1-1/4-mile, $4 million Classic.

Cigar, winner of 17 of his last 19 races, including last year's Classic and racing's all-time money winner, was set as the 4-5 favourite in the early betting line after drawing the seventh post position.
Dare and Go, who has been in the money 19 of 21 career starts, was rated the 6-1 second favourite in the 14-horse field. Dare and Go drew the inside gate.
Three-year-old filly Yanks Music, is moving up to challenge the boys to become the first filly to win the Classic. She was listed at 10-1 in the early betting line.

The Classic also lured the first Japanese horse, five-year-old Taiki Blizzard, to run in the Breeders' Cup since its first year in 1984. He has won five of 12 starts, including both of his races on dirt.

The other races are the $1 million Sprint over six furlongs; the $1 million distaff at 1-1/8 miles; the Mile Turf worth $1 million; the $1 million Juvenile for two-year-olds and the $1 million Juvenile Fillies -- both over 1-1/16 miles -- and the $2 million Turf at 1-1/2 miles.

The Turf races have drawn 12 European horses. In previous Breeders' Cups, overseas horses have had difficulty adjusting to the climates, especially at the warm weather sites. But this year the chilly Canadian weather and the course itself should help them.
The new turf course, laid out two years ago, is 1-1/2 miles long, has wide turns, European-style inclines and the longest home stretch in North America at 1,440 feet (439 meters).
The Breeders' Cup Turf will have four Irish horses to challenge 4-1 favourite Awad with Chris McCarron up, breaking from the 12 chute.

The favourite of the geriatric set in the Turf likely is 5-1 second favourite, Diplomatic Jet, owned by 99-year-old Fred W. Hooper, a two-time winner of the Eclipse Award as best trainer in the United States.
Hooper won the Kentucky Derby in 1945 with the first thoroughbred he ever owned. Hooper's Precisionist won the 1985 Breeders' Cup Sprint.

The Turf also includes 99-1 Ricks Natural Star, a seven- year-old gelding, who should be a natural for last place. His entry is viewed by some as a publicity stunt by owner William Livingstone. The horse has not raced in 14 months and last won in 1993 against $3,500 claimers.
The Mile turf has three horses from Ireland and one from Britain. Da Hoss is the 5-1 favourite.

The class of the Sprint in the early line was Honour and Glory, trained by D. Wayne Lukas, who has 10 horses entered in Breeders' Cup races, showing he still employs a shotgun style approach to big races by entering as many horses as possible.
The Distaff has the day's smallest field with seven fillies. Different, from Argentina, is a slight favourite ahead of Serena's Song, last year's champion three-year-old filly.
Lukas called Serena's Song -- the horse he has dubbed "Her Highness" -- "almost too good to be true. Her consistency gives you a great comfort zone.
"Her and Cigar have typified what we all want in a racehorse," said Lukas, unabashed at comparing his horse to Cigar.
Ordway is the 2-1 favourite in the Juvenile, followed by Boston Harbour, another Lukas horse.
Storm Song is the 5-2 favourite in the Juvenile Fillies, and Lukas's Sharp Cat is the second pick at 7-2.
